extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH-style grant applications / PDs-PIs and senior/key personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and required content for the 'Facilities & Other Resources' and 'Biographical Sketch' portions of an NIH-style grant application, including laboratory/BSL-3 capabilities, equipment, core access, biosafety/compliance, and biosketch formatting and length rules for senior/key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory facilities (Ragon Institute)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ragon Institute laboratory space: more than 80,000 square feet of research and office space; BL2+ containment tissue culture rooms with adequate laminar flow hood space; standard tissue culture equipment including incubators, freezers, centrifuges, automated cell counters and computer access within the tissue culture room; a clean room for PCR adjacent to the tissue culture room and bench space in the open lab available for molecular biology and protein work. Dr Lu has a dedicated tissue culture hood, shared open benches, adequate incubator/refrigerator/-20 freezer/-80 and liquid nitrogen storage space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of specific infrastructure items is provided as evidence of adequate laboratory capacity for the proposed work (BL2+ rooms, laminar flow hoods, dedicated tissue culture hood, dedicated/freezer storage). Explicit mention when animal resources are 'Not applicable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSL-3 facility (Ragon Institute)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ragon Institute BSL-3 laboratory is a 2,240 square foot facility run as a core: dedicated adjacent bench and BSL-2 space, flexible office space, six biosafety cabinets for tissue culture, an enclosed Aria FACS instrument for live cell sorting, a dedicated microscopy room for live cell imaging with a NIKON TiPFFS3 Perfect Focus System Inverted Microscope for time lapse imaging, and a vivarium for conventional and BLT humanized mouse models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSL-3 features and availability (enclosed FACS, live imaging microscope, biosafety cabinets, animal vivarium) should be described to demonstrate the capability to conduct high-containment experiments; list of specialized instruments and dedicated space indicates readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All work in the BSL-3 facility is managed by a dedicated biosafety officer and conducted per institutional protocols approved by the Partners Institutional Biosafety Committee. All work is in compliance with local (Cambridge), state and federal regulations, as well as the NIH Guidelines for Research Involving Recombinant or Synthetic Nucleic Acid Molecules and the CDC Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories guidance document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional oversight (biosafety officer, IBC approval), explicit reference to compliance with NIH/CDC guidance, and citation of relevant local/state/federal compliance to satisfy reviewers that biosafety/regulatory requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel training, competency, and medical clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel have training covering bloodborne pathogens and biosafety, and will be required to demonstrate competency in BSL-3 laboratory work before receiving approval for unescorted access. All BSL-3 personnel will also be required to be medically cleared by the Partners occupational medicine department prior to being allowed to access the BSL-3 laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe required trainings, competency demonstration, and medical clearance procedures (occupational medicine) for personnel; indicate that these are prerequisites for unescorted access to high-containment facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer and office resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Full computer support is available for the PI: dedicated Macintosh laptop with SSD and additional HDD, access to Partners Health Care Systems Network with secure email and institutional libraries, necessary scientific software (FloJo, GraphPad, MatLab, Microsoft Office, R, Stata, CellProfiler, Endnote), additional computing resources including a networked computer within the BL2+ lab space, shared office, dedicated desk, phone, fax/photocopy services, and administrative assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document dedicated computing hardware, network access, and necessary software for data analysis and image processing to show the project has computational/office infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core facilities and technical support
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to core facilities including flow cytometry core with 3 LSR2 flow cytometers and a Fortessa 5-laser cytometer, cell sorting with BD FACSAria High speed sorter, AutoMACS for cell separation, BioRad Bioplex 3D, Biacore, AMNIS Imagestream, CYTOF, fluorescence microscopy core, sequencing platforms (Illumina NextSeq, MiSeq), PCR platforms including Roche LightCycler and Fluidigm, and technical support in flow cytometry and imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List available cores and specialized instruments and note availability of technical support; this demonstrates access to specialized assays and consultative expertise required for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvard School of Public Health laboratory & BSL-3 resources
rubrics_metrics.description: HSPH lab: ~2,000 sq ft BL-2 space and a BSL-3 containment facility used by multiple investigators; major equipment includes Illumina MiSeq, Deltavision live cell imaging, chemostat, PCR machines, Nanodrop, flow cytometers, FACS, Agilent bioanalyzer, plate readers, HPLC, electron microscopy, confocal microscopy, autoclaving and dish washing facilities. The BSL-3 (~1200 sq ft) is divided into procedure rooms, equipment room, animal holding room and office; maintained under negative pressure with redundant exhaust fans; regular power is backed by a generator; systems are monitored and undergo annual checks/certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe shared institutional laboratory space, specialized instrumentation, BSL-3 environmental controls (negative pressure, redundancy, generator), monitoring and certification schedules to demonstrate robust infrastructure and continuity measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and access control
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory area is physically secured by a three-tier system: ID to enter the school, swipe access to enter the floor (granted by PI), and swipe access to enter the BSL-3 suite (issued by laboratory director/manager).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify multi-tiered physical security and controlled access procedures for high-containment areas to show appropriate security measures are in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, user oversight, and health monitoring (HSPH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators undergo intensive training and testing before starting work covering knowledge of pathogen(s), risk assessment, risk mitigation, PPEs, biosafety, good laboratory practices, evacuation, spill control and clean up, incident reporting and health monitoring. All new hires are registered into an occupational health program requiring initial and annual screenings (including TB skin test). The laboratory manager/director and most users have postgraduate degrees and relevant professional memberships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail training curricula, testing, and health monitoring policies (initial/annual screenings) to assure reviewers personnel competence and health surveillance procedures are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment availability, certification, SOPs, maintenance and emergency power
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive equipment inventories are listed (laminar flow hoods, fume hoods, microscopes, centrifuges, sequencers, multiple PCR machines, flow cytometers, ELISPOT readers, -80°C freezers, ultracentrifuges, imaging systems, aerobiology suite equipment, etc.). BSCs are certified biannually and the rest of the equipment is certified annually. All equipment is backed by emergency power. There is a written SOP for each equipment use and maintenance; maintenance is performed after decontamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide inventories, certification schedules (biannual/annual), SOPs for equipment use/maintenance, emergency power/backups, and decontamination-maintenance workflows to demonstrate operational reliability and biosafety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional institutional resources and analytic support
rubrics_metrics.description: Microarray cores are available at various Harvard-associated facilities; statistical support is available at Massachusetts General Biostatistics Core supported by Harvard Catalyst; high-throughput imaging facilities and CellProfiler support are available at affiliated institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List available external cores (microarray, imaging) and statistical support resources to show access to additional services and analytic expertise beyond the home lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified biosketch template and strict five-page limit for each senior/key person; include required headings and content in the prescribed order to avoid administrative noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required biosketch sections include NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME; POSITION TITLE; EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable). For each person, provide Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contribution to Science, and Research Support. 'Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate each required section (education/training with institution, degree, completion date, field of study; personal statement summarizing relevance to project; positions/honors; contributions to science with representative citations; ongoing and prior research support) as described to meet NIH biographical sketch expectations.
